textbookText: Practical Chemistry AgCl + No; cr + AgN03 ---....-..........-....-.-.-.-+ white ppt CO-S- + BaC12 + 2Clwhite ppt Note: Addition ofNH4Cl suppresses ionization of aqueous (NH4)2 C03 due to common ion effect. For this reason, ionic product of the metal carbonate decreases and solubility product becomes greater than its ionic product. That's why MgC03 does not get precipitated out. But, solubility product of CaC03 is very low and still the decreased ionic product value can exceed its solubility product value. Hence, CaC03 gets precipitated out.

Separation of Mixtures Check the completeness of precipitation of CaC03. For this, heat the solution and allow it to settle for some time. Add a drop of (NH4)2 C03 solution to the supernatant liquid. If a fresh ppt appears, add few more drops of (NH4)2 C03 solution.
Check the completeness of precipitation again as before. If no fresh ppt appears, the precipitation is complete.
Filter off the solution. Wash the ppt with a little distilled water 2-3 times.
Take the ppt-washed water from the stem of the funnel in two different test tubes. Add few drops of AgN03 solution and BaC12 solution separately.
Formation of a white ppt with AgN03 solution indicates the presence of chloride ion (NH4Cl or HCl solutions) in the ppt.
Similarly, formation of a white ppt with BaC12 solution indicates the presence of soluble carbonate (NH4)2 C03 or MgC03 solution in the ppt.
If a ppt is seen in any of the test tubes, wash the ppt again.
When no more ppt is seen in both the test tubes, then dry the IO. precipitate in air oven or over the Bunsen burner.
Recovery of magnesium carbonate B. To the filtrate, add excess of ammonium bicarbonate solution. Boil it for some time. MgC03 precipitates out as a white ppt.
Check the completeness of precipitation as before. When the precipitation is complete, then filter off the solution. Wash the ppt with a little distilled water times.
Take the ppt-washed water from the stem of the funnel in two different test tubes. Add few drops of AgN03 solution and BaC12 solution separately.
Formation of a white ppt with AgN03 solution indicates the presence of chloride ion (NH4Cl or HCl solution) in the ppt.
Similarly, formation of a white ppt with BaC12 solution indicates the presence of soluble carbonate [(NH4)2 C03 or MgC03 solution] in the ppt.
If a ppt is seen in any of the test tubes, wash the ppt again.
When no more ppt is seen in both the test tubes, then dry the precipitate in air oven or over the Bunsen burner.

RESULT
CaC03 and MgC03 were separated from their mixture by chemical methods followed by filtration, washing and drying.
PRECAUTIONS
1. The precipitation of CaC03 and MgC03 should be complete.
2. All the glasswares should be handled with care.
3. Care should be taken while drying the ppt over the burner.
